history.period: 1764 CE (built by Swargadeo Rajeswar Singha, r. 1751-1769)
history.summary: CSV DUPLICATE FLAG: CSV row 84 ('Basistha Temple', Dispur) is almost certainly the same temple as this row - no separate Basistha temple is documented at Dispur; only one Basistha Temple exists (at Basistha/Beltola, Guwahati), so the two rows appear to describe one shrine with inconsistent town labels. The Shiva temple stands in the Basisthashram, believed to be the home of sage Vasistha (Basistha), guru of Lord Rama, who is said to have meditated here and whose cave lies ~5 km inside the ashram near a waterfall. The site has remains of a stone temple dated ~1000-1100 CE; the existing octagonal brick temple with a polygonal sikhara (Nilachal architecture) was built by Ahom king Rajeswar Singha in 1764, who also gifted 835 bighas of land to the ashram. The garbhagriha is sunken and said to hold the sage's foot impression. It stands on the bank of the mountain streams (Sandhya, Lalita, Kanta) that become the Basistha and Bharalu rivers. Damaged-structure/repair details vary across sources.

name: Basistha Temple
town_description: Guwahati is the largest city of Assam and the main gateway to Northeast India, set on the banks of the Brahmaputra river. It is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in India (ancient Pragjyotishpura) and hosts several major temples including Kamakhya, Navagraha and Umananda.

travel.airport: Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport - about 25 km west of the temple (verify).
travel.railway: Guwahati Junction railway station - about 14 km (per travel guides; verify).
travel.road: About 10-14 km south-east of the city centre on the Beltola-Basistha road; city buses stop at 'Basistha Mandir'; taxis/autos from anywhere in Guwahati.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March (pleasant and dry); the mountain streams and waterfall are at their best just after the monsoon.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Widely reported as 7:00 AM-9:00 PM (verify). Modest dress, remove footwear; the meditation cave is ~5 km inside the ashram.
